data.get(\"bead_id\").and_then(|v| v.as_str());\n236\t                let outcome = data.get(\"outcome\").and_then(|v| v.as_str());\n237\t\n238\t                if let (Some(bead_id), Some(outcome)) = self.stats.get_mut(&name).and_then(|m| m.get_mut(&version))\n242\t                        {\n243\t                            match outcome {\n244\t                                \"Success\" => entry.successes += 1,\n245\t                                \"Failure\" => entry.failures += 1,\n246\t                                \"Timeout\" => entry.timeouts += 1,\n247\t                                _ => {}\n248\t                            }\n249\t                        }\n250\t                    }\n251\t                }\n252\t            }\n253\t\n254\t            _ => {}\n255\t        }\n256\t    }\n257\t\n258\t    /// Produce a `VariantComparison` for every template that has been observed.\n259\t    pub fn comparisons(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, VariantComparison> {\n260\t        self.stats\n261\t            .iter()\n262\t            .map(|(template_name, by_version)| {\n263\t                let comparison = VariantComparison {\n264\t                    template_name: template_name.clone(),\n265\t                    min_dispatches: self.min_dispatches,\n266\t                    variants: by_version.clone(),\n267\t                };\n268\t ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n287\t// Percentile helpers\n288\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n289\t\n290\t/// Calculate the median (50th percentile) from a slice of values.\n291\t///\n292\t/// The median is the value separating the higher half from the lower half of a data sample.\n293\t/// For an odd number of elements, it's the middle value. For an even number, it's the\n294\t/// average of the two middle values.\n295\t///\n296\t/// # Edge Cases\n297\t///\n298\t/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n299\t///\n300\t/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n301\t/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n302\t/// - **Even number of elements**: Returns the average of the two middle values\n303\t///\n304\t/// # Examples\n305\t///\n306\t/// ## Basic usage\n307\t///\n308\t/// ```\n309\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_median;\n310\t///\n311\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50];\n312\t/// let median = calculate_median(&latencies);\n313\t/// assert_eq!(median, 30); // Middle value\n314\t/// ```\n315\t///\n316\t/// ## Even number of elements\n317\t///\n318\t/// ```\n319\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_median;\n320\t///\n321\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40];\n322\t/// let median = calculate_median(&latencies);\n323\t/// assert_eq!(median, 25); // Average of 20 and 30\n324\t/// ```\n325\tpub fn calculate_median(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n326\t    if latencies.is_empty() {\n327\t        return 0;\n328\t    }\n329\t\n330\t    let n = latencies.len();\n331\t    if n == 1 {\n332\t        return latencies[0];\n333\t    }\n334\t\n335\t    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n336\t    sorted.sort();\n337\t\n338\t    let mid = n / 2;\n339\t    if n % 2 == 1 {\n340\t        // Odd number of elements: return middle value\n341\t        sorted[mid]\n342\t    } else {\n343\t        // Even number of elements: return average of two middle values\n344\t        (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2\n345\t    }\n346\t}\n347\t\n348\t/// Calculate the 95th percentile from a slice of values.\n349\t///\n350\t/// The 95th percentile (p95) is the value below which 95% of observations\n351\t/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the \"tail\" of a distribution\n352\t/// — for example, in latency metrics, p95 tells you that 95% of requests\n353\t/// completed within this time, while the slowest 5% took longer.\n354\t///\n355\t/// # Edge Cases\n356\t///\n357\t/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n358\t///\n359\t/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n360\t/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n361\t/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p95 between the two values\n362\t/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n363\t///\n364\t/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n365\t///\n366\t/// # Algorithm\n367\t///\n368\t/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n369\t/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n370\t///\n371\t/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n372\t/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n373\t/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n374\t/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n375\t/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n376\t/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n377\t/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n378\t///\n379\t/// This method was chosen because:\n380\t/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n381\t/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n382\t/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n383\t/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n384\t/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n385\t///\n386\t/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n387\t/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 95th percentile is approximately `95.5` (rounded to `96`),\n388\t/// not the maximum value `100`.\n389\t///\n390\t/// # Examples\n391\t///\n392\t/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n393\t///\n394\t/// ```\n395\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n396\t///\n397\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n398\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n399\t/// // rank = 0.95 * 9 = 8.55, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.55\n400\t/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n401\t/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.55 = 95.5 → 96\n402\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 96);\n403\t/// ```\n404\t///\n405\t/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n406\t///\n407\t/// ```\n408\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n409\t///\n410\t/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n411\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&unsorted);\n412\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 96); // Function sorts internally → same result\n413\t/// ```\n414\t///\n415\t/// ## Larger dataset\n416\t///\n417\t/// ```\n418\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n419\t///\n420\t/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n421\t/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n422\t///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n423\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&data);\n424\t/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n425\t/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.05 = 190.5 → 191\n426\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 191);\n427\t/// ```\n428\t///\n429\t/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n430\t///\n431\t/// ```\n432\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n433\t///\n434\t/// let single = vec![42u128];\n435\t/// let p95 = needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n443\t///\n444\t/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n445\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&empty);\n446\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 0); // No data → returns 0\n447\t/// ```\n448\t///\n449\t/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n450\t///\n451\t/// ```\n452\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n453\t///\n454\t/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n455\t/// let p95 = 20\n459\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n460\t/// ```\n461\t///\n462\t/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n463\t///\n464\t/// ```\n465\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n466\t///\n467\t/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n468\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&three);\n469\t/// // rank = 0.95 * 2 = 1.9, floor_index = 1, fraction = ```\n474\t///\n475\t/// ## Real-world latency example\n476\t///\n477\t/// ```\n478\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n479\t///\n480\t/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n481\t/// let recommendations\n495\tpub fn calculate_p95(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n496\t    if latencies.is_empty() {\n497\t        return 0;\n498\t    }\n499\t\n500\t    let n = latencies.len();\n501\t    if n == 1 {\n502\t        return latencies[0];\n503\t    }\n504\t\n505\t    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n506\t    sorted.sort();\n507\t\n508\t    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n509\t    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n510\t    // For p95: rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)\n511\t    let rank = 0.95 * (n - 1) as f64;\n512\t    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n513\t    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n514\t\n515\t    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n516\t    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n517\t\n518\t    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n519\t    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n520\t\n521\t    // Round to nearest integer.\n522\t    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 95.5 → 95.4999... → 95).\n523\t    // Standard rounding: 95.0-95.499... → 95, 95.5-96.499... → 96\n524\t    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n525\t    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n526\t}\n527\t\n528\t/// Calculate the 99th percentile from a slice of values.\n529\t///\n530\t/// The 99th percentile (p99) is ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n711\t\n712\t/// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n713\t///\n714\t/// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n715\t/// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p95 percentile.\n716\t///\n717\t/// # Statistical Approach\n718\t///\n719\t/// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n720\t/// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n721\t/// 2. **Calculate one p95** on the pooled data\n722\t///\n723\t/// **Do NOT average p95 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n724\t/// invalid because percentiles are non-linear statistics. Averaging them produces\n725\t/// misleading results.\n726\t///\n727\t/// # Example\n728\t///\n729\t/// ```no_run\n730\t/// use needle::stats::P95Collector;\n731\t/// use Instant::now();\n738\t///     // ... perform work ...\n739\t///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n740\t/// }\n741\t///\n742\t/// // Calculate p95 across all iterations\n743\t/// let p95_us = collector.p95();\n744\t/// println!(\"p95 latency: {} μs\", p95_us);\n745\t/// ```\n746\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n747\tpub struct P95Collector {\n748\t    /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n749\t    samples: Vec<u128>,\n750\t}\n751\t\n752\timpl P95Collector {\n753\t    /// Create a new empty collector.\n754\t    pub fn new() -> Self {\n755\t        Self {\n756\t            samples: Vec::new(),\n757\t        }\n758\t    }\n759\t\n760\t    /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n761\t    ///\n762\t    /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n763\t    /// reallocations during benchmarking.\n764\t    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n765\t        Self {\n766\t            samples: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),\n767\t        }\n768\t    }\n769\t\n770\t    /// Record a single latency sample in microseconds.\n771\t    pub fn record(&mut self, latency_us: u128) {\n772\t        self.samples.push(latency_us);\n773\t    }\n774\t\n775\t    /// Record multiple latency samples at once.\n776\t    pub fn record_all(&mut self, latencies: impl IntoIterator<Item = u128>) {\n777\t        self.samples.extend(latencies);\n778\t    }\n779\t\n780\t    /// Calculate the p95 percentile across all recorded samples.\n781\t    ///\n782\t    /// Returns `0` if no samples have been /// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n1760\t    /// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p99 percentile.\n1761\t    ///\n1762\t    /// # Statistical Approach\n1763\t    ///\n1764\t    /// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n1765\t    /// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single Default)]\n1792\t    pub struct P99Collector {\n1793\t        /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n1794\t        samples: Vec<u128>,\n1795\t    }\n1796\t\n1797\t    impl P99Collector
